purpose: Unapproved branding direction, not a screenshot of implemented software
prompt:
Generate one high-fidelity desktop application UI branding concept for TENET, a local read-only inspector of coding-agent policy decisions. Landscape 1536x1024. Show the actual app edge to edge, not a laptop, poster, mood board, landing page or physical machine. This is concept 1, 'Signal desk'. The design world is a serious laboratory measurement instrument translated into modern software: warm pale gray instrument panels #D8D6CD, porcelain reading surfaces #F4F2E9, very dark olive-black lettering #252725, disciplined vivid vermilion-orange #EF5B2A for the active navigation mark and brand. Extremely refined compact industrial grotesk type, robust numerals, understated monospaced code, thin dark separators and calibration-scale graphics. No faux knobs, screws, glowing tubes, gradients, glassmorphism or ornamental grain. Make it visually distinctive through form and proportions, not decoration. Design a custom geometric TENET wordmark using a restrained paired-gate symbol.

Composition: a shallow, continuous utility header with TENET at left and 'Local archive / Read-only', 'Refresh archive' at right. A dense 230px left index of sessions and recent calls, clean rows with an orange selection tab and a dark outlined selection. Main area uses the rest of the viewport fully, not a narrow article floating in enormous whitespace. At its top a wide charcoal command display with the small readable label 'Shell command' and the exact command 'git status --short && git diff -- README.md && git diff --cached --stat'. Below, a commanding two-part outcome readout: the left two-thirds says 'Would block' in very large dark type beside an outlined stop symbol; its field label is 'TENET decision'. The right third is distinctly separated and says 'Ran', label 'Actual execution', with the explanation 'Observe mode does not enforce decisions.' These are recorded outcomes, never action buttons. The conceptual distinction must be obvious. The broad lower workspace contains 'Why this decision', 'Evidence confidence was below the required threshold.' Then the rule 'Never send any email without confirmation.' with 'Rule at line 5' and a compact GREEN 'PASS' outcome marker. Directly beneath, a precise horizontal ruler-style meter from 0 to 1, filled to 0.85, with an unmistakable threshold line at 0.9. Labels 'Evidence confidence', 'Recorded 0.85', 'Required 0.9'. Green PASS and insufficient evidence must coexist truthfully. Add 'PASS is not a reported violation. The evidence-confidence check did not pass.' Below, compact real disclosure controls: 'Submitted questions', 'Shared evidence', 'All rules', 'Recording details'. The disclosures look like instrument-panel drawers but are normal accessible software affordances, not nested cards.

Sidebar sample calls: selected 'Shell command / Would block', then 'Edit file / Would allow', 'Edit file / Block', 'Shell command / Would allow', 'Edit file / Would ask for approval'. One session 'tenet-observe'. Footer 'Synthetic preview data'. Keep text genuinely legible and coherent. No invented performance metrics, safety guarantees, trend graphs, approval buttons, charts without data, or settings that change enforcement. Aim for the polish of a premium professional design tool with the grounded warmth of a precision instrument. One screen only.
reviewNotes: Branding reference only. Generated green confidence fill must not be copied as a success signal for insufficient evidence; implement amber or neutral with exact meter geometry.
